ORDER 1. All these five cases are disposed of vide this composite order as identical issues are raised therein.

2. Vide these revision petitions, the petitioners have assailed the order dated 08.03.2018, passed by learned trial court in Complaint Case No. 36/16, 46930/2016, 46929/16, 54826/16 and 41853/16,
vide which, after taking the cognizance of the complaint, accused persons were summoned to face trial for the offences under Section 26/52 read with Section 59 of Food Safety and Standards Act,
2006 (FSS Act 2006).
CR No. 360/18, 362/18, 13/19, 361/18 & 284/18 Page No. 1 of 3 3.

sentences.text: Briefly, the case of the prosecution is that on 06.04.2015, the Food Safety Officer visited the Karkardooma area wherein allegedly one Ram Chander was intercepted and was found having stored/meant "Royal Zafrani Zarda" for sale for human consumption.

(Facts are taken from CR No.
360/18).
The sample was taken.
Necessary procedure under Food Safety & Standards Act was thereafter followed.

sentences.text: That on the completion of investigation, vide report dated 21.04.2015, it was found from the report of Food Analyist that the sample was unsafe because it contained tobacco and Nicotine which was prohibited under Regulation 2.3.4 of the Food Safety & Standards (Prohibition & Restriction on Sale), Regulation 2011, and for misbranding to be in violation of regulations 2.2.2.3 of the Food Safety & Standard (Packaging & Labeling) Regulations, 2011.

entities.text: Food Safety & Standards (Prohibition & Restriction on Sale), Regulation 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
A sanction accordingly was obtained from the commissioner Food Safety GNCT on 20.04.2016.
5.
That the complaint was then filed in the court of ACMM for the offence under Section 26/52/59 of Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006.
Cognizance of the offences was taken by the learned ACMM and the accused persons were thereafter summoned to face the trial.
The said order has been assailed by the revisionists in these revision petitions.

6. The main contention of the Revisionists is that the provisions of the FSS Act, 2006 is not applicable to the present case as `Zarda', which is Tobacco product, is not governed by the Food Adulteration Act but in fact it is governed by the Cigarettes and other Tobacco products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution)
Act, 2003.

entities.text:
Cigarettes and other Tobacco products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution)
Act, 2003
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is further submitted that 'Zarda' is a proprietary food and there is no standard for it under the Food Safety and Standard Act, Therefore it cannot apply to the sample commodity.
In these circumstances, the Food Safety Officer has no right to collect the sample and to prosecute the revisionists under the provision of the FSS Act.

7. To buttress his arguments, learned counsel for the revisionists has relied upon the recent judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi titled as 'Food Inspector vs. CR No. 360/18, 362/18,
13/19, 361/18 & 284/18 Page No. 2 of 3 Rupesh Jain & Ors. 2018(1) FAC 145, and other cases tilted as Ram Babu Rastogi and Ors. vs. State through Food Inspector (PFA)2012(1) FAC 56; S. Salem Babu and Anr. vs. The Food safety Inspector 2016(2) FAC 432 and Jayavllas Tobacco Traders LLP vs. The Designated Officer 2017)2) FAC 359.
8. During arguments

sentences.text: , learned SPP for the Department fairly conceded to the law laid down by the authorities relied upon by the revisionists and also the fact that the said orders have thereafter not been assailed by the department before the superior court and thus attained finality.

9. In view thereof, considering the facts and circumstances of the case at hand, in light of the propositions of law enunciated by the above said authorities, in my considered opinion, the case of the revisionists is squarely covered by the authorities relied upon by the revisionists and shall not be governed by the provisions under the FSS Act, 2006 but regulated by the provisions of COPTA.
The complainant has no power to initiate the proceedings against the revisionists under the said Act.

Thus, the impugned summoning order dated 08.03.2018 passed by the learned ACMM is bad in law and cannot be sustained.
10.
Revisions are allowed.
11. Summoning order dated 08.03.2018 stands set aside.
